message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow uses actions that are not certified by GitHub.
# They are provided by a third-party and are governed by
# separate terms of service, privacy policy, and support
# documentation.

name: Elixir CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "main" ]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  codespell:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: codespell-project/actions-codespell@v2
        with:
          skip: deps
          ignore_words_list: tucan
  build:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - elixir: "1.18.2"
            otp: "27.2"
            lint: true
          - elixir: "1.15.6"
            otp: "26.1"

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7

    - uses: erlef/setup-beam@v1
      with:
        otp-version: ${{matrix.otp}}
        elixir-version: ${{matrix.elixir}}

    - name: Restore dependencies cache
      uses: actions/cache@v6
      with:
        path: deps
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-mix-${{matrix.elixir}}-${{matrix.otp}}-${{ hashFiles('**/mix.lock') }}
        restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-mix-

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: mix deps.get
    - name: Compile with warnings enabled
      run: mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors
    - name: Format
      run: mix format --check-formatted
      if: ${{ matrix.lint }}
    - name: Run tests
      run: mix test --cover
      if: ${{ matrix.lint }}",
  "rationale": "The build job has representative successful history (all recent runs complete in roughly one minute), satisfying the P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT precondition that successful job history is representative. The matching experiment applied timeout-minutes: 5 to a similar Elixir/mix CI job and reported all runs still succeeded with modest elapsed savings. Adding a 5-minute bound (about 4x the observed runtime) prevents runaway job consumption without removing any build, format, or test step, so intended coverage is preserved. No permissions, secrets, deployment, or new network access is introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-ishara-pattern-bat-ca499b3aaef0d029"]
}

- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: Cache dependency downloads - modest benefit, preconditions: repeated dependency fetching measurable, cache inputs include lockfile and environment. The workflow already has a cache for deps.

- P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: Cancel superseded runs - needs concurrency group. Could add concurrency. But contraindications: release/deployment work, distinct branches share cancellation group. This workflow runs on push and PR. Could be applicable but requires careful handling.

But the evidence is simulation_estimate.
- P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT: Derive timeout candidates from successful history - there's an experiment example showing adding timeout-minutes: 5 to a workflow.
